answer_1.quote: We next train a language model that takes our edited set of ingredients as input and generates a new set of recipe steps as a single string.

answer_2.quote: We measure fidelity of edited ingredient lists against ground truth, we calculate Jaccard similarity (IoU) and F1 scores , and precision and F1 for insertions and deletions. To measure step fidelity, we compare the workflow of two recipes via Normalized Tree Edit distance (NTED) between structured ingredient-cooking-action tree representations . We measure the fluency of generated directions via ROUGE-L , a metric that assesses n-gram overlap between edited and gold recipe texts. We measure diversity via the percentage of distinct bigrams (D-2) across edited recipes.

answer_4.quote: We survey 672 home cooks to assess the quality of our edited recipes compared to human-written recipes
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators were asked the question 'Does this recipe use ingredients that violate the dietary constraint?' and provided feedback. Cooks recorded 1) how complete the recipe was (i.e. missing ingredients/steps); 2) how difficult it was to infer ingredient amounts; 3) overall difficulty of execution; and 4) if the recipe was appropriate for its target category.
